core_intuitions: Over-training is a deployment-economics bet: training compute is paid ONCE, but inference compute scales with N and is paid on every forward pass forever — so shrink N and pour in ~10x more tokens than Chinchilla-optimal.

The pipeline is a funnel: a much larger raw stream is quality-filtered and deduplicated down to ~20B kept tokens, then tokenized, packed, and sharded — sourcing streams shards on demand, it never fully downloads the corpus.

Packing concatenates many short documents into fixed 2048-token windows to avoid wasting compute on padding, but this demands per-document position-id resets AND intra-document attention masking to stop cross-document attention leakage and RoPE position aliasing.

position_id==0 is the sole document-boundary signal: a single cumsum over it recovers each token's doc_id and reconstructs the exact block-diagonal causal mask — so no separate document-id array ever needs to be stored on disk.

MinHash signature agreement is an unbiased estimator of Jaccard similarity, and LSH banding turns an O(n^2) all-pairs comparison into near-linear bucket lookups; the (bands, rows) split silently sets the near-duplicate detection threshold via an S-curve.
uint16 (2 bytes/token) memmap sharding lets the OS page cache — not application RAM — serve the working set, which is what makes an ~80GB packed corpus trainable on a machine with far less RAM.

new_figures.name: doc-aware-packing-mask
new_figures.concept: How short documents pack into a fixed 2048 window with per-document position resets, and how position_id==0 alone reconstructs the block-diagonal causal attention mask.
new_figures.rationale: This is the chapter's most mechanically subtle and most distinctive teaching — the payoff sentence 'document boundaries and position resets become the same signal' is hard to hold in the head from prose. A single paneled frame that shows the concatenated window, the resetting position ids, the cumsum-derived doc_id, and the resulting block-diagonal causal mask makes the whole mechanism click at once and is fully legible statically.
new_figures.placement: Tokenizing and Packing to 2048 with Document-Aware Attention
new_figures.brief: Reproduce and visualize the chapter's own seq_len=8 worked example so the figure is exact, not invented. TOP BAND: three short documents drawn as rows of token chips, each wrapped with a bos and eos special chip: doc A = [bos a1 a2 a3 eos], doc B = [bos b1 b2 eos], doc C = [bos c1 c2 c3 c4 c5 eos]. Give each document its OWN categorical hue (three distinct theme-safe accent colors from a neutral categorical palette — never semantic red=bad/green=good), and keep bos/eos chips visually marked (e.g. a small notch or bold outline) so specials read as boundaries. MIDDLE: show the greedy concatenation [bos a1 a2 a3 eos | bos b1 b2 | (spill) eos | bos c1 c2 c3 c4 c5 eos] being sliced into TWO fixed windows of 8 chips each — Window 1 = [bos a1 a2 a3 eos bos b1 b2], Window 2 = [eos bos c1 c2 c3 c4 c5 eos]. Make the window boundary a hard vertical divider and show explicitly that document C spills across it (its eos lands in window 2, and doc B's tail is truncated by the boundary) — the spill is the point. Under each window draw two aligned label rows: (1) position_ids, e.g. Window 1 = [0 1 2 3 4 0 1 2], with every reset-to-0 circled/emphasized; (2) doc_id = cumsum(position_id==0), e.g. Window 1 = [1 1 1 1 1 2 2 2]. RIGHT or BOTTOM: an 8x8 attention-mask grid for Window 1, rows = query token i, cols = key token j, filled cell = 'i may attend to j'. The fill pattern must be block-lower-triangular: a lower-triangular 5x5 block for doc A (rows/cols 0-4), a lower-triangular 3x3 block for doc B (rows/cols 5-7), and the off-diagonal blocks EMPTY. Add one callout arrow: query token b2 (row 7) attends to cols 5,6,7 (B's own bos,b1,b2) but is BLOCKED from cols 0-4 (all of doc A), even though A sits earlier in the same physical window. Bottom caption states the payoff verbatim in spirit: 'position_id==0 is the only signal needed — one cumsum recovers document boundaries, so no separate doc-id array is stored on disk.' Everything must sit inside the viewBox with no chip-label clipping; the mask grid cells must be large enough to read the block structure in both light and dark themes.

new_figures.name: overtrain-deployment-economics
new_figures.concept: Why deliberately train ~10x past Chinchilla's compute-optimal token budget: training cost is one-time while inference cost scales with N and recurs on every request, so a smaller over-trained model wins past a break-even serving volume.
new_figures.rationale: The chapter calls this 'the single most important lesson this capstone teaches' and the whole 20B-token budget follows from it, yet it is argued entirely in prose and one equation. A figure that makes the one-time-vs-forever cost split and the cumulative-cost crossover visible turns an economic argument into an at-a-glance intuition.
new_figures.placement: Why Over-Train? 20B Tokens for a 100M-Parameter Model
new_figures.brief: Two coordinated panels. LEFT PANEL ('the two kinds of compute'): a simple ledger contrasting two cost buckets. Bucket 1 = 'Training compute ~ 6ND — paid ONCE' (draw as a single filled bar, labeled one-time). Bucket 2 = 'Inference compute ~ scales with N — paid on EVERY forward pass, forever' (draw as a repeating strip of small identical bars marching off to the right with an ellipsis, to convey unboundedness). The visual metaphor: one big rock you lift once vs a small toll you pay endlessly. RIGHT PANEL ('the crossover'): a schematic line chart, X axis = 'requests served (serving volume)' increasing left to right, Y axis = 'cumulative compute cost'. Two lines: (a) 'Larger model, Chinchilla-optimal (~20 tok/param)' — LOWER intercept (cheaper to train) but STEEPER slope (higher cost per served request because N is larger); (b) 'Smaller model, over-trained (~200 tok/param, ~10x tokens)' — HIGHER intercept (the one-time over-training cost) but SHALLOWER slope (cheaper per request because N is smaller). The two lines cross at a marked 'break-even serving volume'; shade the region to the RIGHT of the crossover and label it 'over-training wins here — inference savings compound'. Use only the illustrative labels present in the chapter: '~20 tok/param', '~200 tok/param', '10x tokens (one-time)', 'inference cost scales with N'. Invent NO benchmark numbers, no axis tick values — the axes are qualitative/schematic. Distinguish the two lines with theme-safe categorical colors AND distinct dash patterns so they are legible in grayscale and in both themes. A one-line takeaway strip along the bottom: 'Spend compute where it's cheap (training, once) to save it where it's expensive (inference, forever).'

new_figures.name: data-pipeline-funnel
new_figures.concept: The end-to-end data pipeline as a narrowing funnel: a large streamed raw corpus flows through filter, dedup, tokenize+pack, and shard stages down to the final ~80GB / ~200-shard packed tensor the trainer reads.
new_figures.rationale: The chapter IS a pipeline, walked section by section, but the reader never sees the whole flow or the volume funnel in one place. An orienting overview figure gives structure to the whole chapter, shows where each code module fits, and makes concrete the 'stream a much bigger corpus, keep a small fraction' idea that motivates streaming over downloading.
new_figures.placement: Sourcing: Streaming Downloads and an Offline Synthetic Fallback
new_figures.brief: A left-to-right (or top-to-bottom) funnel of stages, each stage a labeled box tied to its code module. STAGE 1 SOURCES: show the four-way mix as stacked/weighted inputs — FineWeb-Edu 70% (web), Cosmopedia v2 15% (synthetic), StarCoder 10% (code), FineMath/OpenWebMath 5% (math), with a small note 'streamed on demand; each has a deterministic offline synthetic fallback (sources.py)'. Draw the four sources sized proportionally to their weights so the 70/15/10/5 split is visible at a glance. STAGE 2 QUALITY FILTER (filters.py): note it is DOMAIN-ROUTED — web/synthetic prose take the generic gate, code and math take their own gates (a generic prose filter would wrongly reject them). STAGE 3 EXACT DEDUP (dedup.py): 'hash normalized text, drop repeats.' STAGE 4 NEAR-DEDUP (dedup.py): 'MinHash + LSH banding, drop near-duplicates.' STAGE 5 TOKENIZE + PACK (pack.py): 'byte-level BPE, pack to SEQ_LEN=2048, doc-aware mask + position reset.' STAGE 6 SHARD (shard.py): 'uint16 memmap .bin, ~100M tokens/shard.' STAGE 7 DATASET (dataset.py): 'PackedMemmapDataset -> training tensor.' The FUNNEL/volume story must be visible: the mouth of the funnel is a wide 'raw stream (a much larger corpus — quality filtering + dedup discard the large majority)' narrowing through filter and dedup, then the packed output annotated with the chapter's illustrative figures: '~20B kept tokens', '~90GB kept raw text', '~80GB packed on disk (40GB tokens + 40GB positions)', '~200 shards (~400MB each)'. Keep boxes evenly spaced with clear directional arrows and no overlapping labels; the module filenames should sit as small monospace captions under each stage. Theme-safe accent per stage but a single restrained palette; must fit fully inside the viewBox.

new_figures.name: minhash-lsh-band-scurve
new_figures.concept: The LSH banding S-curve: how the (bands, rows) split — not just performance — silently sets the near-duplicate detection threshold, and why candidate generation is deliberately decoupled from the final Jaccard re-check.
new_figures.rationale: The chapter's 'Common pitfall' warning argues purely in numbers that band/row choice changes recall, but an S-curve is a shape you must SEE to internalize. Plotting the candidate-probability curve for two band choices, marking the annotated points, and separating the loose candidate stage from the strict threshold=0.8 decision makes the pitfall — and the reason for the two-stage design — immediate.
new_figures.placement: Deduplication: Exact Hashing and MinHash Near-Duplicates
new_figures.brief: A single line chart (follow the dataviz skill for styling, gridlines, legend, and theme-safe palette). X axis = 'true Jaccard similarity J' from 0 to 1; Y axis = 'P(pair becomes an LSH candidate)' from 0 to 1. Plot the banding formula P = 1 - (1 - J^rows)^bands for TWO configurations, both with num_perm=128: curve A = (bands=16, rows=8), curve B = (bands=8, rows=16). Curve A has its steep transition near J~=0.71 (the (1/16)^(1/8) approximation); curve B is shifted RIGHT with transition near J~=0.88 ((1/8)^(1/16)). Distinguish the two curves with categorical color AND dash pattern, legend labeling each with its (bands, rows) and approximate threshold. On curve A, place three annotated markers taken directly from the chapter text: J=0.5 -> ~0.06, J=0.7 -> ~0.62, J=0.8 -> ~0.95. Draw a vertical reference line at J=0.8 labeled 'final drop decision — estimate_jaccard re-check (threshold=0.8)'. Shade/annotate the band-16 curve's rising shoulder around J~=0.7 as 'candidate generation (deliberately loose — over-generates candidates)'. Add a short caption making the decoupling explicit: 'Banding over-generates candidates near J~=0.7; the explicit threshold=0.8 re-check on the full signature is what actually decides a drop. Fatter bands (8x16) raise the threshold and catch fewer near-duplicates; thinner bands lower it.' Keep annotations from overlapping the curves; ensure both curves and the reference line are legible in light and dark themes.

summary: This capstone data-pipeline chapter is concept-rich but has ZERO figures, so this is a build-from-scratch plan (no audits needed). I propose four disciplined figures mapped to the chapter's core intuitions. Two priority-1 flagships: (1) doc-aware-packing-mask — a static paneled reproduction of the chapter's own seq_len=8 example showing packing, position resets, cumsum-derived doc_id, and the block-diagonal causal mask, which makes the chapter's most subtle and distinctive mechanism ('position_id==0 is the only boundary signal') click at once; and (2) overtrain-deployment-economics — a static two-panel (one-time-vs-forever cost split + cumulative-cost crossover) visualizing 'the single most important lesson this capstone teaches.' Two priority-2 supports: (3) data-pipeline-funnel — an orienting stage-by-stage funnel tying each code module to the volume narrowing from a large raw stream down to ~80GB / ~200 shards; and (4) minhash-lsh-band-scurve — an S-curve plot making the 'band/row choice silently changes recall' pitfall visible and separating loose candidate generation from the strict threshold=0.8 re-check. All briefs stay within theme-safe, in-viewBox, statically-understandable, illustrative-numbers-only constraints.
